claims.text: The Global Positioning System relies on a constellation of orbiting satellites broadcasting continuous radio signals with precise timestamps and orbital parameters.
A GPS receiver calculates its distance from a satellite by multiplying the speed of light by the time delay between signal transmission and arrival.
A receiver requires signals from at least four satellites to simultaneously resolve three-dimensional position and correct the receiver clock bias.
Satellite atomic clocks run slightly faster than Earth-based clocks due to general relativity and must apply relativistic adjustments to maintain positioning accuracy.
